★ NOTE: The clinical distinction between upper and lower motor neuron disorders in infants is blurred because\nincomplete myelination of the developing nervous system limits expression of many of the cardinal signs,\nsuch as spasticity.
The course of ALS is progressive, with motor impairment due to either upper or lower motor neuron loss, or both.
Motor pathways and upper versus lower motor neuron lesions
“How would you differentiate an upper motor neuron from a lower motor neuron lesion on exam?” (Spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski vs. flaccidity, fasciculations, atrophy)

Motor exam (strength grading, tone): Upper motor neuron signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski) indicate cord involvement above the level of the lesion; lower motor neuron signs (flaccidity, fasciculations) suggest anterior horn cell or nerve root compression.

qs.q: All of the following are true regarding lower motor neuron lesions EXCEPT:
o: They may lead to noticeable muscle wasting.
They are linked with decreased muscle tone.
They may result in reduced or absent reflexes.
qs.e: Spastic paralysis is characteristic of upper motor neuron lesions. Lower motor neuron lesions commonly cause weakness, reduced tone, muscle wasting, fasciculations, and reduced reflexes.
